aboli-bel: Aboli (Crossandra) flowers don't wilt — they hold their colour for days, which is why they're woven into hair gajras.
fiddle-leaf-ficus-lyrata: The fiddle leaf fig is named for its violin-shaped leaves — and each leaf can grow bigger than a dinner plate.
soleirolia-soleirolii: Soleirolia is called 'baby's tears' — a single plant spreads into a cushion of thousands of tiny leaves.
office-time-plants-holder: The Office Time plant thrives on neglect — fluorescent light and missed waterings barely slow it down.
portulaca-yellow: Portulaca is the 'sun rose' — its flowers open with the morning sun and close again at dusk, every day.
pachira-aquatica: The money tree's braided trunk is made by braiding several young stems together while they're still flexible.
ficus-small-netted-bonsai: Ficus bonsai are among the easiest bonsai — they tolerate indoor life and forgive missed waterings.
ficus-netted-bonsai: Ficus trees can live for centuries — some of the world's oldest bonsai are over 800 years old.
madhukamini-bonsai: Madhukamini bonsai fill a room with orange-blossom fragrance — a flowering bonsai is a rare thing.
banyan-tree-bonsai-bud: The banyan is among the largest trees on Earth — one tree in Howrah spreads over 14,000 square metres of canopy.
ficus-bonsai-m: Ficus latex was once used as rubber — early rubber production drew on Ficus trees before the rubber tree took over.
dasylirion-serratifolium: Dasylirion is called 'desert spoon' — its long, toothed leaves were used as brushes by Native Americans.
kaner: Kaner (oleander) is one of the world's most poisonous plants — and one of the most indestructible roadside bloomers.
dieffenbachia: Dieffenbachia is called 'dumb cane' — its sap temporarily numbs the tongue, a built-in defence against nibblers.
dacena-mahatma-pinkish-red: Dracaena colour cultivars like 'Mahatma' are bred for leaf colour alone — they trade speed of growth for beauty.
